summary: Jean Przyluski was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics who studied under Henri Hubert and Marcel Mauss at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and the École Nationale de la France d'Outre-Mer. He held professorships at INALCO, EPHE, and Collège de France.

Jean-Baptiste Biot was a French physicist and scholar of history and archaeology who studied at Lycée Louis-le-Grand, École des Ponts ParisTech, and École Polytechnique. He held long-term professorships at the Collège de France (1800–1862) and the Science Faculty of Paris (1809–1862).

Jean-François Jarrige was an archaeologist and Indologist who studied at Lycée Claude Fauriel, École du Louvre, and the University of Paris. He served as director and head of the Guimet Museum from 1986 to 2008.

Jean-François Lyotard was a philosopher who studied at Lycée Louis-le-Grand, the University of Paris, and Paris Nanterre University. He held academic posts at Paris Nanterre, Paris 8 University Vincennes-Saint-Denis, UC Irvine, and Emory University.
Jean-François Revel was a philosopher who completed his studies at Lycée Jean-Baptiste-Say, Lycée du Parc, and the École Normale Supérieure.

Jean-Louis Burnouf studied at Lycée Saint-Louis and under Alexander Hamilton and Antoine-Léonard Chézy. He held posts at Lycée Louis-le-Grand, the École Normale Supérieure, the University of Paris, and was chair of Latin eloquence at the Collège de France (1816–1844).
Jean-Luc Achard is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and held a post at the Centre national de la recherche scientifique.

Jean-Luc Chevillard is an Indologist and linguist who studied at the École Normale Supérieure and under Antoine Culioli. He held posts as a researcher at the CNRS from around 1990 and as a lecturer at the University of Hamburg around 2008.

Jean-Noël Robert is a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and sinology who studied under Bernard Frank and at INALCO. He held posts at the CNRS, the École Pratique des Hautes Études, and served as professor at the Collège de France (2011–2022).

Jean-Pierre Abel-Rémusat was a sinologist and linguist who studied at INALCO under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy. He held the Chair of Sinology at the Collège de France (1814–1832) and served as conservator at the Bibliothèque nationale de France.

Jean-Pierre Drège is a scholar of sinology and Buddhist studies who studied at INALCO, the University of Burgundy, and under Yves Hervouet. He served as president of the École française d'Extrême-Orient from around 1998 to 2004.

Jeannine Auboyer was an art historian and Indologist who studied at the École du Louvre, EPHE, and University of Paris under scholars including Joseph Hackin and René Grousset. She served as chief curator at the Guimet Museum and held a chair at École du Louvre.

Jeff Dolven studied at Yale University and the University of Oxford. He served as a fellow at Harvard University and Trinity College, Cambridge, before becoming a professor of English at Princeton University around 2001.

Jeff Malpas is a philosopher who studied at the University of Auckland and the Australian National University. He led the philosophy programme at Murdoch University and served as professor and emeritus distinguished professor at the University of Tasmania.
Jeff Shore is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. He served as a professor at Hanazono University from around 1987 to 2019, where he became professor emeritus.
Jeff Watt is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and history and archaeology who studied under Dezhung Rinpoche Kunga Tenpai Nyima. He held a post at the Rubin Museum of Art.
Jeff Wilson is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies who earned his PhD from the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill and studied under Taitetsu Unno and Myosei Tatsuguchi.

Jeffery D. Long is a scholar of religious studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Notre Dame and the University of Chicago, and became an associate professor of religion and Asian studies at Elizabethtown College in 2000.

Jeffrey Broughton is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology who earned his PhD from Columbia University. He was attested in 2004 as a professor in the Department of Religious Studies at California State University.

Jeffrey Clark Ruff is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied at Missouri State University and UC Santa Barbara under David Gordon White. He taught at UC Santa Barbara, was a director at the University of California, and joined Marshall University in 2002.
